_meta.method: original literal English gloss from the Sanskrit commentary; Sanskrit order preserved; no machine-translation prose

1.translation: The Lord has described the form of the Supreme Lord to be worshiped through Chapters 7–9, and has briefly shown His manifestations through statements such as “I am the taste in water,” “I am the sacrifice,” and “I am the rite.” Now, wishing to elaborate those same manifestations so that the Lord may be seen everywhere, and wishing to describe why devotion to Him must be practiced, He said: “Again, O mighty-armed one, hear My supreme word, which I shall speak to you, who take delight in the nectar of My words, out of a desire for your welfare.”
word_for_word: the form of the Supreme Lord to be worshiped
take delight in the nectar of My words
to you out of desire for your welfare

2.translation: The devas and great sages such as Bhṛgu do not know My exalted origin—My manifestation through many glories—even though I am unborn. For I am the beginning and cause of the devas and the great sages in every way, both as their producer and as the one who sets their understanding and other faculties in motion. Therefore no one knows Me without My grace.
word_for_word: the one who sets the intellect and the rest in motion

3.translation: Whoever knows Me as unborn, beginningless, and the great Lord of the world, undeluded among mortals, is freed from all sins.
word_for_word: the great Lord of the world

4.translation: Śrīdhara further makes clear the Lord’s status as the great Lord of the world: intelligence is skill in discerning the essential from the nonessential; knowledge is knowledge of the Self; non-delusion is freedom from agitation; patience is endurance; truth is speaking what is real; restraint is control of the external senses; tranquility is control of the inner instrument; happiness is agreeable experience; suffering is its opposite; being is arising; non-being is its opposite; fear is terror; and fearlessness is its opposite. All these qualities arise from Me alone.
word_for_word: skill in discerning the essential from the nonessential

5.translation: Nonviolence is cessation of causing pain to others; equality is freedom from attraction and aversion and equal regard for friend and enemy; contentment is satisfaction with what is obtained through providence; austerity is the bodily and other discipline described later; giving is offering lawfully earned wealth to a worthy recipient; fame is good reputation and disgrace is bad reputation. These and their opposites—intelligence, knowledge, and the rest—are the many states of living beings that arise from Me alone.
word_for_word: cessation of causing pain to others
freedom from attraction, aversion, and the like
equal regard for friend and enemy
satisfaction with what is obtained through providence

6.translation: The seven ancient great sages, beginning with Bhṛgu, and the four sages before them, beginning with Sanaka, as well as the Manus beginning with Svāyambhuva, are My manifestations: they were born from My mind by the mere power of My resolve. From these sages and Manus arose the people of the world—appropriately as children, grandchildren, descendants, students, and the like.
word_for_word: born from My mind by the mere power of My resolve
in the form of children, grandchildren, and the like
in the form of disciples and the like

7.translation: Whoever knows in truth these manifestations of Mine, such as Bhṛgu and the others, and this yoga characterized by lordly power becomes joined to unwavering yoga, to right vision, without doubt.
word_for_word: characterized by Bhṛgu and the others

8.translation: “I am the source of the entire world; everything proceeds from Me.” I am the cause of its origin through manifestations such as Bhṛgu, and from Me proceeds every state described earlier—intelligence, knowledge, non-delusion, and the rest. Understanding this, the wise, endowed with loving feeling, worship Me.
word_for_word: I am the source of everything
through manifestations in the form of Bhṛgu and the others
intelligence, knowledge, non-delusion, and the like

9.translation: Their minds are in Me; their lives are dedicated to Me, or their senses have gone to Me. Such wise devotees instruct one another about Me using reasoning supported by scripture and other means of knowledge, and continually speak of and chant about Me. They become satisfied through mutual approval and encouragement, and they rejoice, attaining fulfillment.
word_for_word: whose lives are dedicated to Me
whose vital powers have gone to Me alone
with means of knowledge supported by reasoning
with scripture and the other means of knowledge

10.translation: To those who are constantly united with Me, attached to Me, and worship Me with love, I give that buddhi-yoga—the means in the form of understanding—by which they reach Me.
word_for_word: of those who are of this kind

11.translation: Having given them buddhi-yoga and brought it to the point of direct experience, I destroy the darkness called saṃsāra, born from ignorance, solely out of compassion for them. Where do I abide and by what means do I destroy it? Abiding in the state of the Self, in the movement of the intellect, I destroy it with the shining lamp of knowledge.
word_for_word: abiding in the state of the Self
abiding in the movement of the intellect
with a lamp characterized by knowledge

12.translation: Arjuna said: “You are supreme Brahman, the supreme abode, and the supreme purifier. You are the eternal Person, divine and self-luminous, the primal Deity, unborn, and all-pervading.” Śrīdhara presents these as the opening praises of the Lord’s manifestations that follow.
word_for_word: the primal Deity / first among gods

13.translation: All the sages—Bhṛgu and the others—the divine sage Nārada, and likewise Asita, Devala, and Vyāsa declare You to be so; and You Yourself are declaring it to me.

14.translation: Therefore my doubt about Your lordly glory has now ceased. I regard as true everything You tell me, Keśava, including that the devas and great sages do not know Your origin. Indeed, the devas do not know Your manifestation as undertaken for our blessing, and the demons do not know it as undertaken for their subjugation.
word_for_word: for the sake of blessing us
for the sake of subjugating us

15.translation: “You alone know Yourself through Yourself, O Supreme Person. O source and nourisher of beings, O Lord of beings, O God of gods, O Lord of the world.” Śrīdhara explains that no other person knows the Lord through any other means; each form of address states a reason for His supreme status—as creator and nourisher of beings, their ruler, the illuminator of the gods, and protector of the world.
word_for_word: O creator and nourisher of beings
the god / illuminator of the gods beginning with the Sun

16.translation: Since You alone know Your manifestation, not the devas and the others, You alone are qualified to explain all Your divine and wondrous manifestations—the glories through which You pervade these worlds and remain present in them.

17.translation: Arjuna asks the purpose of the detailed account: “How may I know You, O Yogī, by continually contemplating You? Through which different manifestations should I contemplate You, and in which objects are You to be thought of by me, O Blessed Lord?”

18.translation: Therefore, O Janārdana, tell me again in detail about Your yoga—the lordly power characterized by omniscience and omnipotence—and Your manifestations. Even though I am outward-facing, let my mind become absorbed in thinking of You here and there through the different manifestations; I never become satisfied when I hear Your nectar-like words.
word_for_word: characterized by omniscience, omnipotence, and the like

19.translation: The Blessed Lord said: “Good; out of compassion I will tell you the divine manifestations of Myself, O best of the Kurus, in their principal forms. There is no end to the detailed extent of My manifestations, so I will describe only some of the chief ones.”

20.translation: “I am the Self, O Guḍākeśa, abiding as the inner controller in the inner instruments of all beings through qualities such as omniscience. I am the beginning—their birth—the middle—their continuance—and the end—their dissolution—of all beings.”
word_for_word: in the inner instruments of all beings
the cause of birth and the rest

21.translation: “Among the twelve Ādityas I am Viṣṇu, Vāmana; among lights I am the radiant sun with rays that pervade the world; among the Maruts I am Marīci.” Alternatively, Marīci is one of the seven groups of wind-deities. “Among the stars I am the moon.” Śrīdhara notes that the genitive here sometimes indicates the principal member of a group and sometimes a relation; even incarnations such as Viṣṇu are called manifestations because the intent is to indicate exceptional glory.
word_for_word: endowed with rays that pervade the world
